title: Volume 1 Chapter 7: I Don't Understand Love 2
content: "It takes this long to travel by horse. Just how isolated are the villagers?"
I muttered, and Krush nodded as she looked up at the rocky mountains from her mount.
"I sense something unusual is happening. Lord Salt, this village might not be an ordinary place."
Her words made me tighten my grip as I turned my gaze toward the village entrance.
This village, with the rocky mountains towering behind it, seemed like a closed-off place where crops wouldn't grow and the land was barren.
The entire village had a somehow dark atmosphere, and the air felt heavy.
"Let's go, Krush. We need to assess the situation first."
We dismounted and stepped into the village.
The villagers looked unwell, as if afflicted by illness, their eyes mixed with wariness and anxiety as they stared at us.
It was clear that this was no ordinary sickness.
"We are members of the Fourth Knight Order of Corias. We've come to investigate the illness spreading in the village,"
Krush addressed the villagers, but at first, everyone showed expressions of confusion.
They were unsure whether to trust us.
However, when I demonstrated my ability to use Healing Magic, their attitudes began to change.
"Did you really come to help us? The Knight Order of Corias?"
An elderly man approached us, looking skeptical.
"Yes. I can use Healing Magic. First, please show me your conditions. I will do my best to treat you."
At my words, the villagers expressed their gratitude and bowed deeply.
Gradually, more villagers approached and began to share their situations with us.
"The rumors about an unknown illness might be true..."
I murmured, and Krush looked around with a serious expression.
"Something is definitely off in this village. Is it just my imagination, or does the air feel heavy?"
While there was no distinct stench of Miasma, the thick atmosphere was palpable.
"...Thank you. We truly appreciate it. People have been collapsing one after another, and we have no means left..."
At those words, Krush nodded firmly.
"We will investigate thoroughly. And we will find a way to save the village."
The villagers began to trust us gradually, slowly introducing us to those who were afflicted by the illness.
The entire village was suffering, and it was evident that those who had lost family and friends were sinking into despair.
Krush and I walked around the village, casting purification and healing spells on each house.
I poured all my strength into helping, hoping to make a difference.
With each spell I cast, I could see a glimmer of hope returning to their faces, which encouraged me as well.
However, when I stopped in front of one house, I noticed a different atmosphere.
From inside, I could hear the sound of quiet sobbing.
I exchanged glances with Krush and quietly opened the door.
Inside, I found a girl, consumed by sorrow.
She looked to be around ten years old, curled up on the floor, crying.
Next to her lay two corpses.
"...Was it already too late?"
The sight of the girl who had lost her parents pierced my heart painfully.
Her figure reminded me of Asha and Cynthia from the past.
Our village was attacked by monsters, and I had fled with the two of them.
The girl before me had been unable to escape, forced to witness her parents' deaths.
As I approached her, trying to find words to comfort her, she noticed me and opened her eyes wide, shouting.
"Why! Why didn't you come sooner!? My father and mother weren't saved! Why!?"
Her anger was directed at me.
She hurled her sorrow and despair at me for not being able to save her parents.
I could only accept her words in silence.
Thinking of the girl's grief made my own powerlessness sting deeply.
"...I'm sorry."
I could only quietly apologize.
Because I had arrived too late, I couldn't save her loved ones.
That was the truth.
Not knowing what to say to the girl who continued to cry, I searched the house.
In the back room, I found her sister lying on a bed.
I quickly checked her condition and found that she still had a faint breath, so I immediately cast Healing Magic.
"Please, let it be in time..."
I infused my magic, performing purification and healing simultaneously.
After a while, the sister's breathing stabilized, and I could see her complexion gradually improving.
She slowly opened her eyes and looked at me.
Surprised, she seemed confused about the situation as her sister hugged her tightly.
"Sister!"
Though the sister had awakened, the younger girl continued to cry.
The sorrow of losing their parents must have been tightening her heart.
I had managed to save the sister, but I couldn't heal the younger girl's emotional wounds.
"I'm sorry. I couldn't save your father and mother... truly."
I bowed my head in apology to the sister, who was still trying to grasp the situation.
The girl cried even harder, tears flowing endlessly, while the sister finally understood and continued to stroke her head.
Krush stood by silently, watching our exchange without saying a word.
After surveying the village, we ended up spending the night there.
However, the regret of not being able to save the girl's parents weighed heavily on my heart, so I shook off those feelings and headed into the forest.
Once I entered the woods, an unnatural silence enveloped the area, just like in the village.
Normally, I would hear the sounds of creatures and the wind, but here, there was nothing.
The silence echoed heavily in my heart.
Amidst this, I suddenly heard the sound of water.
I was drawn to the sound and walked toward it.
As I made my way through the trees and reached the water's edge, there was Krush.
She was bathing in the water, her bare skin enveloped by the clear water.
The moonlight quietly poured down in the stillness of the forest.
The light reflecting off the water shimmered, revealing Krush's figure.
Her silver hair sparkled as if sprinkled with stardust, gently swaying in the water.
Her well-trained body was wrapped in smooth, white skin.
While possessing the sharpness and strength of a warrior, her skin also conveyed a feminine softness, accentuated by the moonlight.
Her muscles were gracefully defined, evoking a sense of exquisite craftsmanship.
Water flowed down her body, yet she showed no sign of feeling the cold.
Krush stood silently under the moonlight, as if blending into the tranquil night and becoming part of nature.
Her silver hair spread across her back, reflecting the light and softly glowing.
That sculpted body was both a testament to her pride as a warrior and, under the moonlight, it exuded a sense of fragility.
I momentarily held my breath at the sight before me.
Krush was not just a knight who fought.
I felt an indescribable emotion welling up in my chest, stirred by her beauty and quiet strength, but I quickly pushed that feeling down.
Startled, I accidentally stepped on a twig, and our eyes met.
"I-I’m sorry!"
I hurriedly averted my gaze and turned away.
I had been entranced by her stunning beauty.
I felt my face heat up, realizing how rude I had been.
"It's fine. There's nothing lost by being seen naked."
However, Krush seemed completely unconcerned.
Her voice was calm.
Her nonchalant words left me a bit taken aback.
I found myself responding as if I were scolding Asha.
"No, that's not the issue! As a woman, you should have a little modesty."
I said this without turning around, but I regretted that I was the one saying it after peeking.
Yet, Krush appeared unfazed, and the gentle sound of water resumed.
"Modesty...?"
Her voice suddenly sounded quiet.
"You have that kind of feeling, Lord Salt?"
But I don't understand that feeling.
I may not have had the luxury to feel modesty, having spent my time training and fighting as a knight.
At her words, I finally realized that her indifference was not mere carelessness.
She might have suppressed such emotions to become stronger and protect herself.
I had no words to respond to that.
Krush quietly emerged from the lake, illuminated by the moonlight, casually drying herself.
I was momentarily at a loss for words, but I regained my composure and once again offered my apologies.
"I'm really sorry for earlier..."
Krush glanced at me for a moment but then shrugged and replied in her usual calm tone.
"I truly don't mind. Even if you saw me naked."
I almost opened my mouth at her words, but realizing her attitude was genuinely indifferent, I swallowed my words.
I suddenly felt a sense of discomfort at her calmness.
How could she remain so unperturbed? Or was there something else she was feeling?
"But... I can't understand. As a woman, you should cherish your body more. I feel sorry for having seen it."
Krush seemed to ponder my words for a moment, slowly responding while drying herself.
You have that kind of feeling, Lord Salt.
But I don't understand it.
On the battlefield, there often isn't time to hide one's body, and being naked doesn't mean losing anything.
I'm just cleansing myself now.
At her words, I momentarily gasped.
I couldn't truly grasp whether Krush genuinely thought that or if she simply didn't feel something.
Suddenly, the events of the day flashed through my mind, and I wanted to delve deeper into her heart.
I wanted to know what she was feeling and thinking.
"I see... Hey, Krush."
"Yes?"
Today, being blamed by the girl for not being able to save her parents is really bothering me.
If I had come to the village sooner, I might have been able to save her parents.
Thinking about that...
I was venting my frustrations while searching for the right words.
I have Holy Attribute and can use purification and healing magic, but it's not always in time.
For that girl, it was too late for me to come to her aid.
Krush fell silent for a moment but eventually replied in a calm tone.
"That's just how it is. Not everyone can save everyone. I've seen such scenes many times."
Her words surprised me.
It felt as if she was speaking while completely detaching her emotions.
And just as I was about to say something more, Krush quietly added,
"I don't understand love."
At that single statement, I instinctively looked up.
"...You don't understand love?"
Krush gazed at me, her serious eyes continuing.
I lost my parents before I could even comprehend.
I have no memories of receiving affection.
I feel indebted to Lady Freina and Lady Rana, and I want to protect the members of the Knight Order.
But I don't know if that is 'love.' Honestly, I can't understand the feelings of the girl who cried after losing her parents today.
I was at a loss for words.
Her voice lacked emotion, merely stating facts.
Yet, within that, a sense of loneliness lingered.
"Krush..."
I didn't know how to respond to her words and simply stared at her.
Krush's eyes were fixed on me, but there was something missing that felt different from her usual calmness.
"One day, you'll come to know love."
"Will such a time come?"
I couldn't weave any more words beyond that.
Before dawn, the sky began to take on a slight blue hue, and the village was quietly preparing to greet the morning.
However, suddenly piercing through that tranquil atmosphere, a shrill scream echoed.
"GYAAAAAA!"
The air-splitting cry jolted me awake.
"What the!? Is that a monster's cry?"
I immediately dashed outside, and before me was a scene of countless monsters surrounding the village.
"The village is under attack!?"
I was startled but quickly sprang into action.
Krush, awakened by the earlier scream, was already armed with her sword.
I headed toward the village's defense.
Near the entrance, massive monsters emerged from the darkness, and the villagers were frozen in fear.
I drew my dagger and took down a nearby monster.
Looking around, I saw villagers fleeing in panic, and the sisters I had helped in the evening huddled together in fear.
"Krush! Protect those sisters!"
I rushed toward the girls at the edge of the village.
They were the sisters who had just lost their parents.
Now they were once again exposed to the monsters' attack.
"Leave it to me!"
Krush stood in front of the two, readying her sword.
The monsters charged toward us, embodying terror, attempting to overwhelm Krush and the others with their overwhelming strength.
"I will definitely protect you...!"
The sisters watched as Krush braced herself against the approaching monsters with her shield.
But there were too many of them.
No matter how many times she swung her sword, the monsters kept coming.
Krush fiercely swung her sword, pushing back the monsters, but suddenly she was struck from behind with a powerful impact.
Before she could turn around, Krush collapsed to the ground, and the monsters closed in.
"Damn it..."
Krush seemed unable to move, her eyes closed.
If she lost consciousness now, it would be a disaster.
But before I could get closer, I heard the sisters' screams.
They had thrown themselves over Krush, desperately trying to protect her with their small bodies.
I plunged my dagger into the monsters to shield the three of them.
But with so many monsters, the blood loss was mounting.
I realized how difficult it was when no one was there to guard your back, feeling the terror of battle.
The older sister weakly threw stones at the monsters, while the younger sister held Krush's hand tightly, tears welling in her eyes.
"Help! Big brother!"
For a moment, the faces of Cynthia and Asha flashed in my mind, and in response to their cries, I unleashed a burst of Holy Attribute magic.
The Holy magic filled the entire village, healing Krush and reinforcing my own body with enhancement magic.
I had no choice but to settle this quickly.
"I will... definitely protect you!"
I swung my dagger and faced the monsters.
"Lord Salt?"
With her wounds healed, Krush regained consciousness.
"Are you awake?"
She seemed surprised to see the two girls clinging to her.
"They threw themselves over you to protect you."
"Why would they do that?"
"Who knows? Perhaps that's something only those who understand 'love' can do."
"Lord Salt! There's blood on your head!"
"I want to protect you all too! This is nothing!"
Though I tried to sound cool, I was reaching my limit.
But I would risk my life to protect Krush and the girls.
With my last ounce of strength, I swept away the monsters.
I didn't care how Krush would feel about it.
I just wanted to help Krush and the sisters.
"Is this... love? The power of the heart to protect someone?"
Krush had said she couldn't understand 'love.'
Could that really be true?
If she couldn't understand love, then she wouldn't understand gratitude or kindness either.
Yet, she felt indebted to Lady Rana and Lady Freina.
She treated Mei kindly as a subordinate.
The actions of the sisters unfolding before me were the very essence of 'love.'
The girls, having lost their parents, were risking their lives to protect Krush.
"Why... why are you trying so hard...?"
I couldn't tell what Krush was feeling.
But tears naturally flowed down her cheeks.
Despite saying she didn't understand what love was, Krush's emotions were clearly grasping the meaning of the sisters' actions.
The darkness gradually lifted, and the morning sun began to rise from the eastern sky.
As the battle settled down, I finally recognized the true nature of the monsters that had attacked us.
"Zombies..."
As I whispered that, I saw decaying orcs and ogres attempting to assault the village with their grotesquely twisted bodies.
They were zombies, exuding a foul odor from their rotting flesh, their eyes gleaming with a lifeless, dark light.
But now that the darkness had dissipated, we finally had the leisure to comprehend the situation.
"Krush, are you okay?"
Seeing Krush, who had been down, protected by the sisters, I hurried to her side.
Though her breathing was ragged, it seemed she had no major injuries.
"I'm fine... Lord Salt, I... I want to..."
Krush gently stroked the heads of the two girls.
It seemed there was affection in her gesture.
"It's not over yet. Let them rest."
"Ah, Lord Salt! Look over there!"
Krush pointed, and there were still zombies approaching the village.
Though there were few, if left unchecked, they would pose a threat to the village again.
"If they are zombies, then it's my job with Holy Attribute magic. Leave it to me. Krush, take care of them."
"Ah, please do. I'm your knight protector."
"People help each other. Just watch my Holy magic; I will purify them."
I steeled myself and activated the Holy magic with the remaining magic power.
Zombies could rise again even if defeated with regular weapons.
To completely drive them away, only purification with holy power would suffice.
"HOLY CIRCLE!"
I spread my arms wide, casting a holy barrier that enveloped the entire village.
A pale blue light wrapped around the village, and as the orc zombies and ogre zombies touched that light, they let out pained groans as their bodies crumbled to ash and vanished.
"This is... the end."
As the sun began to rise, peace and tranquility returned to the village once more.
The purified land no longer bore the ominous shadows of zombies, and the village was saved.
"Krush, it's okay now. We've saved the village."
Krush wobbled to her feet, and upon hearing my words, she nodded slightly.
She looked tired, but relief was evident in her eyes.
"Thank you, Lord Salt... and to them as well."
The sisters, tears in their eyes, seemed to lose consciousness, perhaps from relief.
I sat down, feeling relieved for the village we had saved and the lives that remained unharmed.
"Now the villagers can live in peace."
I felt a sense of relief for having saved the village with my own power, but my heart felt heavy knowing there were lives I couldn't save.
However, I told myself that I should rejoice in having protected this peace for now.
